files.purpose: New in B3: a @MainActor generic registry, PendingReplies<Value: Sendable>, that parks one CheckedContinuation<Value, Error> per string request id so a stdio provider can await the reply line carrying that id. It factors out the hand-rolled continuation dictionaries that B2 kept separately in ClaudeSession (pendingControl, throwing) and PiSession (pendingResponses, non-throwing with a 30 s timer), and adds two things B2 did not have there: task-cancellation support (withTaskCancellationHandler plus an up-front Task.checkCancellation) and bulk resume (resolveAll/failAll). The doc comment (lines 3-4) states the ordering guarantee: the id is registered before `send` runs, so a fast reply cannot arrive before anyone is waiting.
key_symbols: func register(_ id: String, timeout: Duration? = nil, timeoutValue: Value? = nil, send: () -> Void) async throws -> Value (10-36)
@discardableResult func resolve(_ id: String, _ value: Value) -> Bool (38-43)
@discardableResult func fail(_ id: String, _ error: Error) -> Bool (45-50)
calls_into: Task { } unstructured timer task inheriting the main actor (22-29)
Used by B3 DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:37,306,338,340,684 (PendingReplies<JSONValue>, no timeout; fail/resolve on control_response; failAll on close)
Used by B3 DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:57,266,290,594 (register with timeout .seconds(30), timeoutValue .null; resolve on response; resolveAll(.null) on close)
state_owned: continuations: [String: CheckedContinuation<Value, Error>], main-actor isolated, keyed by request id; an entry exists from registration until it is removed by resolve, fail, resolveAll, failAll, the timeout task, or the onCancel task
side_effects: register stores the continuation under id (line 19) BEFORE invoking send() (line 20); send is invoked synchronously on the main actor inside the continuation body
If the calling task is already cancelled on entry, Task.checkCancellation() (line 17) throws CancellationError before anything is registered or sent, so send() never runs

With a timeout, spawns an unstructured Task (lines 22-29) that sleeps for the duration (try?, so it proceeds even if that timer task were cancelled) and then either resolve(id, timeoutValue) when a timeoutValue was given, or fail(id, CancellationError()) when it was not (doc comment line 9); both are no-ops returning false if the id was already removed
The timer task captures the PendingReplies instance strongly (self.resolve / self.fail) for the timeout duration

On task cancellation after registration, onCancel spawns a main-actor Task holding self weakly that removes the id and resumes the continuation by throwing CancellationError (lines 32-34); the removal is asynchronous (hops to the main actor), and a reply that wins the race is delivered normally because removeValue then returns nil
resolve/fail remove the entry first and resume only if present, returning true when an entry was found and false otherwise (lines 39-50)
resolveAll/failAll snapshot all waiting continuations, clear the map, then resume each (lines 52-62), so resumption never touches a map being iterated

Registering an id that is already present overwrites the dictionary slot (line 19) and orphans the earlier continuation, which is never resumed (a leaked CheckedContinuation); both B3 callers use monotonically increasing counters so this is not reached by them
platform_assumptions: Swift structured concurrency semantics: withTaskCancellationHandler runs onCancel immediately when the task is already cancelled, and concurrently (on an arbitrary executor) when cancelled later, which is why the handler hops to the main actor
Unstructured Task { } inherits the main-actor context and task-locals but not the parent's cancellation, so the timeout timer is not cancelled when the awaiting task is
feature_notes: Status A: the file does not exist at B2 (1fbf81e6); git diff B2..HEAD shows 63 insertions, which is the whole file.

Refactor source: B2 ClaudeSession.swift:37 held `pendingControl: [String: CheckedContinuation<JSONValue, Error>]`, B2 :306-308 used withCheckedThrowingContinuation directly, B2 :337-342 removed-and-resumed on control_response, and B2 :686-690 drained the map on close. B3 replaces all of that with PendingReplies<JSONValue> (B3 :37, :306, :338, :340, :684).

Refactor source: B2 PiSession.swift:62 held `pendingResponses: [String: CheckedContinuation<JSONValue, Never>]` (non-throwing), B2 :265-273 armed its own 30 s timer that resumed with .null, and B2 :304 resolved by id. B3 PiSession :266 calls `try? await pendingResponses.register(id, timeout: .seconds(30), timeoutValue: .null)` and returns `value ?? .null`; :290 uses the Bool from resolve to fall through to the failed-prompt branch.

Behaviour change for Claude control requests (ClaudeSession.control): B2 was not cancellable (spec PR-PROVCLI-042 records `cancellation: not cancellable`). B3 throws CancellationError without sending the control_request when the calling task is already cancelled, and throws CancellationError (removing the pending entry) when the task is cancelled while waiting. Claude callers at B3 :219, :224, :246, :266, :296 wrap control in try?, and :160 (initialize) propagates the throw.

Behaviour change for Pi requests (PiSession.request): B2's only bound was the 30 s timer (PR-PROVCLI-276 `cancellation: The 30 second timer is the only bound.`). In B3 a cancelled caller gets JSON null (CancellationError swallowed by try?, then `?? .null`), and a caller whose task is already cancelled gets JSON null without the request line ever being written. The 30 s timeout still resolves with JSON null, never throwing.

Behaviour change for Pi close: B3 PiSession.didClose (:594) now calls pendingResponses.resolveAll(.null) FIRST, so every waiting request (get_state, get_commands) returns JSON null immediately on process exit instead of waiting out the 30 s timer as in B2 (B2 didClose :638-653 never touched pendingResponses).

No behaviour change for the Claude close path in outcome: B2's inline snapshot/clear/resume-throwing loop is now pendingControl.failAll(ProviderError.failed(reason ?? "Claude exited.")) with the same order and error.
Minor lifetime difference: B2 Pi's timer task captured PiSession strongly for 30 s; the B3 timer captures only the PendingReplies instance. Not user-observable.
No spec record cites this new file; the observable changes above surface through records that cite ClaudeSession.swift and PiSession.swift, which belong to those files' bundles.
unresolved_questions: Whether any B3 call path actually cancels the task awaiting ClaudeSession.control or PiSession.request (for example a start task cancelled during initialize or get_state) is a question for the ClaudeSession/PiSession/caller bundles; this file only makes cancellation possible.
